**Date:** 2026-10-30 · **Scan basis:** WangLabCSU/msuiter @ origin/main `2296f49` (P10 parity-lane merge; local `main` one commit behind at `43a5db9`) · **Prepared for:** Nature-class paper pillar-1 (architecture & implementation), standing doctrine RB-10/P-1/G5 (measurement/evidence methodology banked as ours; algorithmic originality deferred to the perf phases, now adjudicated here).

## 2. Per-element verdict with citations

### E2 KL-MU NMF kernel — **Verdict (c): prior art, comprehensively**
The KL/EU multiplicative MM updates are Lee-Seung 2001 / β-divergence Févotte-Idier 2011 (module docs themselves cite these, `nmf.rs:16-33`). Production instantiations in this exact domain: SigProfilerExtractor's consensus KL-NMF pipeline (Islam et al., *Cell Genomics* 2022, DOI 10.1016/j.xgen.2022.100179 [P] per the extractor README), R `NMF` brunet (the numerical-protocol reference target itself, `docs/research/09` §3 G1), MutationalPatterns ([M] companion papers Genome Medicine 2018, DOI 10.1186/s13073-018-0539-0; BMC Genomics 2022, DOI 10.1186/s12864-022-08357-3), rust-NMF's GPL bit-equivalent port ([P] README: brunet/lee/offset/nsNMF "bit-equivalent", 76–280×, `github.com/omicverse/rust-NMF`). **The ε-policy deserves a footnote, not a claim:** upstream SigProfilerExtractor 1.5.0 (2026-09-28) independently shipped the alternative fix — a 1e-16 floor *on* W/H/W@H with NaN/inf replicate rejection ([P] CHANGELOG raw fetch); msuiter's division-only-ε + zero-frozen-dead-component design is a defensible *variant* of known art, and the paper should cite the 1.5.0 CHANGELOG to show the landscape was surveyed.

### E3 NNDSVD init + in-house SVD — **Verdict (c): prior art**
NNDSVD/NNDSVDa come from the Cichocki–Struzek line (not re-verified on-page [U]; the fact that rust-NMF ships `nndsvd`/`nndsvda`/`nnsvd` and attributes its 76–280× to "HALS+NNDSVD" is [P]-verified evidence that the initialization technique is established, published art). Randomized-SVD defaults (q=3, +16 oversampling) are the Halko–Martinsson standard recipe (module doc names it, `nndsvd.rs:8-13` [repo text]). The exact one-sided Jacobi SVD is careful engineering (Boutsidis–Gallopoulos 2008 SVD-init lineage is [M]-confirmable, DOI 10.1016/j.patrec.2007.09.010 — note the returned venue is Pattern Recognition, a different record than the Pattern Recognition Letters 2015 follow-up, DOI 10.1016/j.patrec.2015.05.019) but nothing novel for a genomics audience. **Do not put NNDSVD in the abstract.**

### E1 Two-tier Rust architecture — **Verdict (b): novel combination; no novel primitive**
Rust-FFI-into-R is established (rextendr itself, the repo's own dependency; savvy is the sibling framework [U]). Rust compute cores for signature analysis exist upstream in Python-adjacent form (rust-NMF ships as the `nmf-rs` PyO3 wheel, [P]). The crates.io scan for "mutational signature" and "cancer genomics" returned **zero** signature/NMF crates ([P] crates.io API queries of this scan) — closest are format/variant tools (`vcf-reformatter`, `vardictrust`, `cfdnalab`) and the generalist `bio` 4.2.2 crate ([P] crates.io API: "A bioinformatics library for Rust", 1.17M downloads). So: **there is no prior-art Rust signature-extraction engine in the R ecosystem**, but the defensible novelty is the *certification regime around* the core (forbid-unsafe engine contract + FFI directionality witness + frozen dependency budget + per-call pools + MSRV pin), not "we wrote Rust". Frame as engineering assurance, cite rextendr honestly.

### E4 Frozen RNG streams — **Verdict (b): novel combination**
PCG (O'Neill) and SplitMix64 (Steele–Lea) are published parts [U]; the paper's contribution candidate is the *discipline*: a named, versioned stream layout published in Methods, cross-toolchain bit-identity golden tests, thread-invariance `identical()` gates, and the deliberate rejection of the `rand` ecosystem for reproducibility (ARCHITECTURE §11 risk row 1; `rng.rs` docs). No genomics tool known to expose its RNG stream algebra at all; the field's prior art treats seeds as opaque (the parity plan's G7 row documents sigminer doing exactly that). Novel-combination; useful to the attestation narrative, not a standalone claim.

### E5 Isolated-process batch bridge with frozen protocol — **Verdict (b): novel combination; strongest pure-engineering element**
Process isolation around an FFI boundary is a known reliability idiom in R (sigminer's own `reticulate`/Python-shelling precedent, `R/sigprofiler.R`, documented in `docs/research/09` §2; callr; pandoc shells). What no located prior work has: a *frozen version-stamped file protocol* (protocol=1, breaking-changes-bump-the-number) with self-describing `trace_len`, `%{:.17e}` bit-exact round-trip, handshake-once-per-unit, batch face with per-case receipt attestation, exit-status-by-value law against the silent-kernel-death hazard (forensics bake-death #7, `kernel-pipeline.R:6-9`), and a measured 2.3004× bridge-face speedup (A0 0.14060 s/run → A3 batch 0.06112 s/run; per-k 2.74/2.43/2.19/2.04) delivered with cross-route bit-identity — commit `2296f49` message, numbers banked at `/tmp/perf10lane/logs/00..22` + `budget.tsv`. No citable prior art found in this scan; related practice is generic (IPC protocol versioning). Novel combination — but this is a *methods-section* asset, not a headline result: reviewers will see plumbing, so it earns its place as the mechanism that makes the attestation claims (E6, E11) executable.

### E6 Bit-identity attestation apparatus — **Verdict (a): genuinely novel for this domain**
No mutational-signature (or adjacent genomics-compute) tool found in this scan that constructs cross-route byte-identity proofs with constructed-perfect/constructed-broken firing controls as a CI-resident law family. The general software-testing concept (metamorphic testing / regression oracles) is the closest named prior art [U — not re-verified in this scan; cite the metamorphic-testing literature at manuscript stage]; but its instantiation as *signature-kernel acceptance law* (W/H/meta witnesses identical across binary generations, endpoints-vs-full-trace face identity, monotonicity with committed slack, fault classes re-firing at every change) has no located antecedent. This element shares the banked RB-10/P-1/G5 record with E11 and should be argued as *that* record's kernel-side half. The paper must define "bit-identical" precisely (frozen platform, fixed toolchain, single-thread, fixed loop order) to survive adversarial review.

### E7 Engine registry — **Verdict (b): novel combination**
Model-interface registries are old (tidymodels-class uniform interfaces, S3/S7 dispatch, engine plug-ins everywhere). The distinctive bits: governance fields on the registry row (`certified`, `contract_version`), "data, not a class explosion", an extension contract elevated to a vignette, and the D15 parity doctrine (parity engines of all mainstream methods, one-line swap, *own* calibrated methods as default). Novel-combination platform claim only.

### E8 Calibrated inference layer — **Verdict: the scientific core, with named risks**
- **Coverage-measured exposure intervals (MSU-Fit headline):** **(a) genuinely novel — conditional on the G0 leading experiment surviving.** The domain's own benchmarks state the problem openly: Medo et al., *Nat Commun* 2024, 12-tool fitting comparison, DOI 10.1038/s41467-024-53711-6 [M] (repo corpus: Medo explicitly raised the untested-coverage open question, `docs/research/00-executive-summary.md` §2); Jiang et al., 13-tool benchmark incl. PASA, *Brief Bioinform*, DOI 10.1093/bib/bbaf042 [M]. A negative-search posture (this scan found no tool publishing empirical-coverage curves for signature exposures; conformal-interval queries returned only generic conformal literature) supports (a) but is weak evidence. **Adjacent prior art that reviewers *will* raise:** MSA — simulation-based reproducible attribution *with confidence* (Senkin, *BMC Bioinformatics* 2021, DOI 10.1186/s12859-021-04450-8 [M]) — must be differentiated: MSA gives simulation-calibrated confidence for attribution, not coverage-audited intervals reported over the full N × entropy grid. Bayesian-exposure prior art abounds: BASCULE (*Genome Biol* 2025, DOI 10.1186/s13059-025-03835-9 [M], bioRxiv 2024 preprint 10.1101/2024.09.16.613266 [M]), sigfit (bioRxiv 2018, DOI 10.1101/372896 [M]), Bayesian selection and refitting of reference signatures (*Ann Appl Stat* 2026, DOI 10.1214/26-aoas2138 [M]), mSigHdp HDP rare-signature sensitivity (*NAR Genomics & Bioinformatics* 2023, DOI 10.1093/nargab/lqad005 [M]). The differentiator is *frequentist empirical-coverage verification as product feature*, not another Bayesian point estimate. The repo's own kill-criterion (ARCHITECTURE §10: "a competitor publishing calibrated CIs") shows the team already knows this is the fragile crown jewel — **run the G0 leading experiment to completion before writing the word "first."**
- **Conformal per-TMB-stratum intervals (MSU-LowCount):** **(a), pending formal scan.** No conformal-prediction-for-signature-exposures prior art surfaced (negative search only; conformal-in-biomedicine exists generically). The sub-100-mutation panel/ctDNA fitting gap is corroborated by the corpus (SigMA covers only SBS3/HRD [U]) and the Medo open-question row. Conformal prediction itself is published art (Shafer–Lernsted, Angelopoulos–Bates); novelty = the Mondrian-by-N-bin application + coverage verification on stratified simulations *and* retrospective real panel data — the latter needs the real-data artifact (see gaps).
- **CoDA/DM-mixture exposure association (MSU-Infer):** **(b).** DM/logistic-normal mixture differential abundance reproduces Morrill 2025 [U — the ARCHITECTURE §5 row itself says "reproduce and extend", which is an honest (b) posture]; compositional-data tooling exists (propr-class work [U]). The survival/longitudinal/hurdle extension list is the novel-combination remainder. "First exposure-association framework covering survival/case-control/longitudinal" is claimable only after a dedicated CoDA-in-signatures scan; treat as (b) today.
- Presence testing (NB χ²₁ LRT + BH) and CV K-selection are themselves prior art (Self–Liang boundary theory; SUITOR entry-wise 10-fold CV K selection, *PLoS Comput Biol* 2022 18(4):e1009309, DOI 10.1371/journal.pcbi.1009309 [M]) — msuiter's D13 four-piece-kit calibration protocol (generative model, estimand, coverage curve, sanity harness) is the differentiator, not the statistic.

### E9 Six-modality unified tally — **Verdict (b): novel combination; moat already narrowing**
Every individual modality has prior art *in R alone*: sigminer ships SBS96/DBS/ID/TSB, CN40/CN48 (Tao mutex), SV32-style features, pLOH/aneuploidy ([P] the CRAN package record, cran.r-project.org/web/packages/sigminer/index.html [P] v2.4.0, authors incl. Wang/Tao/Li; inventory in `docs/research/09` §2). SigProfiler-side is no longer blind either: CN/RNA-SBS reference matrices ship in the Alexandrov-lab mirror and the Extractor emits SV matrices (corpus rows, `docs/research/05` [repo-verified]; CHANGELOG-confirmed for 1.5.0 era in `docs/research/09` §3 G12) — the repo's own §8 note 3 already flags this "quiet narrowing of the moat". Also note SigProfilerAssignment (de Bruin et al. 2021 assignment paper, Genome Medicine, DOI 10.1186/gm1228 [U] — publisher redirect observed, final page 404'd through this scan's fetcher) and MuSiCal (*Nature Genetics* 2024, DOI 10.1038/s41588-024-01659-0 [M]) and CANCERSIGN (2018, DOI 10.1101/424960 [M]) and MutSignatures (*bioRxiv*/2020, DOI 10.1101/2020.03.15.992826 [M]) on the tooling flanks. Novel-combination only: one object model + bit-compat channel semantics + skip-ledger provenance across six modalities *with* the Rust substrate. Do not claim breadth as novelty against 2021-era papers; claim it against the *combination*.

### E10 refdb governance — **Verdict (b)**
The mirror-bundling practice is field-standard (SigProfilerAssignment mirror bundles the Alexandrov-lab BSD-2 matrices, per the corpus and the mirror's own role in the SigProfiler stack). The commit-SHA-pinned, manifest-burned, fail-closed, build-independent-relabel, zero-COSMIC-in-repo enforcement package is a genuine governance combination with no located prior-art equivalent [negative search]; useful in a software-family/journal-code paper, not a result.

### E11 Evidence/benchmark methodology — **Verdict (a) per standing doctrine; no prior-art competitor located**
The scan found no genomics-benchmarking publication that combines: single-authoritative-shot campaigns with fired-probe ledgers, co-tenancy load censuses, sealed floor tables with epoch digests, per-row hardware pins, frozen-simulator identity (seed 20260928, `Seeds.txt`), MEASURED/UNMEASURED/FIRST-MEASUREMENT-ONLY citation classes, and a shared oracle between twin campaigns (`bench/m7/tools/verify_campaign.py`). Adjacent prior art lives in *reproducibility* and *benchmarking* papers (Medo 2024 and Jiang bbaf042 [M] are benchmarks without attestation regimes; containerization is common [e.g., nf-core practice, unattested here]). This is the banked RB-10/P-1/G5 originality and pillar-1 can lean on it: **the paper's most defensible one-line identity is "a measurement-and-attestation regime for signature kernels and their claims",** with the Rust core as its instrument.

### E12 (context) NN/deep extraction flanks — **prior art exists, correctly declined**
MUSE (Genome Biol 2016 [U]), SigNet (Genome Biol 2020 [U]), CLIP (Nat Biomed Eng 2021 [U]), Sonata (2025, Park lab [U]) plus this scan's [M] confirmations: supervised NB-NMF (Bioinformatics 2020, DOI 10.1093/bioinformatics/btaa473), NB-NMF model selection (BMC Bioinformatics 2023, DOI 10.1186/s12859-023-05304-1), deep-unfolded NMF (J Comput Biol 2022, DOI 10.1089/cmb.2021.0438), linear-autoencoder/NMF equivalence (J Comput Biol 2025, DOI 10.1089/cmb.2024.0784), BayesMSNF (bioRxiv 2023, DOI 10.1101/2023.03.28.534619), SigFormer attention decomposition (2026 preprint, DOI 10.64898/2026.01.20.700228). The corpus's verdict "no credible winner / no investment" (docs/research/00 §2) stays correct, and Related Work must cite this scan's [M] set so reviewers see the terrain was walked.

## 3. Strongest defensible novelty narrative for pillar-1

Pillar-1 should **not** claim a new factorization algorithm (KL-MU, NNDSVD, Hungarian consensus, SUITOR-style CV-K are all (c)-class prior art, §2). It should claim, in this order:

1. **Certified-compute architecture (E1+E4+E5+E6, combination-level novel):** an R-facing mutational-signature engine in which the numeric core forbids `unsafe` and FFI by construction, thread count and parallel schedule provably cannot move a bit (fixed-order reductions, thread-invariance `identical()` laws), RNG streams are published as named layouts with cross-toolchain golden tests, and the *production call surface* is a frozen-versioned, receipt-attested, bit-identical protocol — demonstrated to be able to buy real time (2.3004× measured on the product bridge face, committed with 822 new law expectations in #62) without moving a single output byte.
2. **The attestation regime as method (E6+E11, the banked RB-10/P-1/G5 original):** constructed-perfect/constructed-broken firing controls, sealed single-shot campaigns, co-tenancy and hardware attestation, and citation-class discipline (MEASURED/UNMEASURED/FIRST-MEASUREMENT-ONLY) — the property that lets the paper *itself* carry no unverifiable number (the house zero-fabrication law is already embodied in `docs/PERFORMANCE.md`'s path:line-quotation design).
3. **Calibration-first inference enabled by 1+2 (E8):** the domain's benchmarks say exposure uncertainty is unvalidated (Medo 2024, open question; Jiang bbaf042 shows point-estimate failure rates); msuiter ships coverage-measured interval reporting, calibrated presence testing, conformal low-count mode, CoDA-aware association — "fast *so that* statistical honesty is affordable" (ARCHITECTURE §10's own framing). Novelty here is conditional on G0 completion (§4 risk R1) and must keep its D13 four-piece kit visible.
4. **Platform grammar (E7+E9+E10):** one object model across six modalities with bit-compat channel semantics and governance-fielded engine registry as the methodological-comparison substrate.

One-sentence draft: *"msuiter's originality is architectural and evidential rather than algorithmic: it is the first mutational-signature stack whose kernel, randomness, and measurements are individually attestable bit-for-bit — and the calibration audits that this makes affordable are the ones the field's own benchmarks declared missing."*

## 4. Gaps and risks for pillars 2 and 3 (with the evidence the codebase already commits)

### Pillar 2 — performance & benchmark
- **R1 (the parity gate is BREACH).** The ≤2× SigProfiler-parity target (P-1 gate) is **MEASURED-FALSE**, not pending: sealed verdict `bench/results/p6_regen_20261016-011928/result.md:6` ("FAIL — 18 offending class(es)", ratios 22.166–67.102); defensible post-correction worst-class 35.0× (688.16 s vs 19.65 s, five-gate P7-F ruling V1, `docs/research/09` §9). The P10 lane moved the *bridge* face 2.30× toward the needed 6.7×; the system-level breach is pipeline-floor bound (~170 s finding, five-gate structural section). **Consequence:** the paper may not carry a SigProfiler-parity claim in any table until a post-P10 full-table regeneration closes it; the honest present claim is "bridge overhead now 2.30×-reduced, bit-identical, with the residual localized to pipeline floor — forensics committed." Memory's PF forensics (bridge share 33.4%, 2× measured-foreclosed for bit-identical code) is a /tmp-lane record, not committed — **re-land it in `bench/` or cite it only as an internal ruling.**
- **R2 (kernel speedups vs C-class baselines are small).** The committed authoritative table: catalog 2.6× / KL-NMF 2.3× / batch NNLS 1.8× vs already-optimized C/Python baselines, with the original 50×/100×/10× rhetoric explicitly moved to a naive-R/Python framing (`docs/PERFORMANCE.md:20-35`, PI ruling 2026-10-05; the ≥100× bootstrap row is MEASURED-false at 15.37×, `docs/PERFORMANCE.md:68-109`). "Rust is faster than R" will not carry a Nature-class perf pillar against C-kernel baselines; pillar-2's differentiated value must be the *attested* end-to-end pipeline numbers, the sigminer-vs-msuiter kernel story (20–45× on the M7 table, `docs/research/09` §1.2), and the forensics discipline — and must re-check the naive-baseline 50× claim on the pinned bench before quoting it.
- **R3 (synthetic-only, one host).** All campaign data is the frozen G0 simulator (seed 20260928); the real-data G0 primary run is blocked on the author's COSMIC v3.6 file (`G0_CATALOG_PATH`, `docs/research/09` §5 P7); headline m1s numbers are single-session on one developer machine with power state uncontrolled (`docs/PERFORMANCE.md:111-130` self-declares this). The mitigations already committed: docker-adapter fairness half with image digests + frozen thread caps (`bench/results/p6_regen_20261023-044026/judgment_m7_degraded_...md`), host/hw_profile row stamps, GO-05 anchors, co-tenancy censuses. Pillar-2 needs at least one real-cohort timing column and/or the G0 primary run.
- **R4 (no GPU story).** GPU replication is an explicit non-goal (`docs/research/09` §6.2) while SigProfiler 1.5.0 runs GPU replicates (corpus G11/GPU rows). Fine if the paper never claims absolute-speed dominance; dangerous if it does.
- **R5 (existing benchmarks).** Medo 2024 and Jiang bbaf042 already own "we benchmarked the tools"; pillar-2 differentiates only through the attestation regime (E11) and the TP-only Hungarian judgment law — Related Work must cite both.

### Pillar 3 — application case studies
- **R6 (synthetic case studies).** Phase-8 committed `bench/scenarios/` (atlas, HRD, treatment) with outputs (`out/hrd_report.csv`, `out/treatment_timing.csv`, `synth-cn.tsv`, …) and law tests (`test-scenario-atlas.R`, `test-scenario-hrd.R`, `test-treatment-report.R`, `helper-treatment.R`); the treatment-forensics design devlog is `docs/devlog/2026-10-28-p8-treatment-forensics-design.md`. These are *demonstrations on simulated cohorts*. The diagnostic-grade claims (MUTYH/MSI panel detection, RNA-only cohort, treatment-record concordance) are gated on cohort collaborations that do not yet exist — ARCHITECTURE §10 lists "no cohort collaboration before M3b" as a pivot trigger. **Pillar-3 as committed today is a methods-demonstration pillar, not a clinical one; the paper must frame it that way or acquire the cohort.**
- **R7 (competitor baselines for the scenarios).** HRD must be benchmarked against HRDetect/SigProfiler-assignment on identical inputs (HRDetect coefficients are already a bit-for-bit golden target, ARCHITECTURE §7.1 — good); per-signature TSB/RTT and treatment-deconvolution "near-zero competition" claims come from the corpus (`docs/research/00` §2 post-processing) and are only [U]-attested — run the same scan treatment before printing "first".
- **R8 (byte-exact HRD claim is against our own ground truth).** The HRD/pLOH/aneuploidy fidelity reference is the sigminer tree (memory: sigminer local ground truth, CRAN 2.3.3) — i.e., the byte-exactness bar is set against the team's own prior package; an independent reference must be added or the claim relabeled.
